mainEvent.title: Wed 11/25 · Hot inflation, a steep morning selloff and a late comeback before Thanksgiving
mainEvent.body: Wednesday's data came in hot and strong: core PCE rose **3.3%** on the year vs 3.2% expected, Q3 GDP was revised up to **4.3%**, claims fell to 189K and new home sales jumped 14.2% to **701K**, the most since December 2025. Stocks opened sharply lower as the AI selloff spread from Asia and the administration proposed new tariffs on 16 trading partners; around 11:00a the S&P 500 fund (SPY) was down 2.8% and the Nasdaq 100 fund (QQQ) 4.4%, and the Dow was down more than 1,100 points at its worst. Buyers came back through the afternoon: the S&P 500 closed **−0.25%**, the Nasdaq **−0.62%**, and the Dow (+0.33%) and Russell 2000 (+0.78%) finished higher. The Beige Book said prices rose moderately and input costs outpaced selling prices. A 25bp hike on December 9 stays almost fully priced. Markets are shut Thursday and close at 1:00p Friday; OPEC+ meets Sunday and the Fed's pre-meeting blackout starts Saturday.

stories.title: Futures jump for Black Friday as Beijing pledges to back its stock market and chips rebound across Asia.
stories.body: S&P 500 futures were up **1.6%** and Nasdaq 100 futures **2.3%** at 8:37a, with Dow futures +1.3%, ahead of a session that ends at 1:00p (site feed, ZeroHedge, TipRanks). China's State Council made a rare midday pledge to channel more long-term money into stocks, give the state-backed "national team" a bigger buying role and push companies toward dividends and buybacks; the Shanghai Composite closed **+3.7%** at about 3,607, the Shenzhen Component +7.2% and the CSI 300 about +4.2% (Trading Economics, ZeroHedge, Ted Pillows). Chip stocks led the rest of Asia after a bruising week for AI shares: the Kospi rose **4.3%** to 4,916, the Kosdaq about 6.7%, and the Nikkei about 2% (Ted Pillows, Wisevoter via InvestingLive, site feed). Europe's STOXX 600 was up about 1.1% by midday. Treasuries reopened lower: the 10Y was about 4.90%, up 5bp (site feed, TipRanks). Gold rose about 3.8% to near $3,670. The 8:30a data showed the October goods trade deficit widening to **$149.5B** vs $133B expected, as imports rose 6.1% to a record on capital goods, and wholesale inventories rose 0.9% vs 0.5% expected (ActionForex, Breaking The News, TipRanks). Adobe expects Black Friday online sales of $12.9B, up 9.2% (via Nexus Research). The Fed's pre-meeting blackout starts Saturday, with a 25bp hike on Dec 9 almost fully priced.

stories.title: Stocks claw back a steep morning selloff as chips slide again and the Dow finishes higher.
stories.body: The AI selloff spread through Asia overnight (Kospi **−6.2%**, Taiex −4.8%, Nikkei −2.8%) and hit Wall Street at the open: around 11:00a the S&P 500 fund (SPY) was down **2.8%** and the Nasdaq 100 fund (QQQ) **4.4%**, and the Dow was off more than 1,100 points at its worst (StockTitan, Motley Fool, AP via KSAT). Buyers came back through the afternoon as yields fell: the S&P 500 closed **−0.25%** at 7,182.78, the Nasdaq **−0.62%** at 23,585.80, while the Dow rose 0.33% to 50,182.95 and the Russell 2000 0.78% to 2,705.84 (Vista Partners, Motley Fool, Longbridge). Nvidia fell **3.9%** to $149.30, its third straight drop since Monday's 31.5% jump to $165.05 on Jensen Huang's return; Micron lost 4.5%, Lam Research and Sandisk about 6%, and AMD, Micron, Marvell and Intel were each down more than 9% at the lows (StockTitan, Longbridge, 247 Wall St., Vista Partners). Among megacaps, Amazon fell 3.1% and Alphabet 2.1% while Meta rose 3.4%. Materials (XLB) gained 2.1% and tech (XLK) lost 0.8% (sector ETFs). Anthropic (**ANT**) rose 1.1% to $82.79 after trading as low as $79.65, still just below its $83 IPO price (StockTitan, Motley Fool). Polymarket's odds of Nvidia ending 2026 above $4T with Huang as CEO are about 36%. Still open for Nvidia: the SEC accounting review reported last week and the 10-Q due Dec 4.

stories.title: The administration proposes new tariffs on 16 trading partners, with 20% on China.
stories.body: The US Trade Representative proposed new duties on 16 major trading partners after an investigation into industrial subsidies and excess manufacturing capacity: **20%** on China and **15%** on the European Union, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, with other rates for Southeast Asian exporters (MarketScreener, StockTitan, Vista Partners). Semiconductors, autos, steel and aluminum are excluded, and the duties aren't expected before January; the US-China trade truce runs out Jan 10 (Vista Partners). Public comments are due Jan 5 and hearings start Jan 25 (StockTitan). MarketScreener says the duties are meant to replace tariffs the Supreme Court struck down earlier this year. The proposal added to the morning selling, but stocks recovered most of the losses by the close; sources differed on some smaller countries' rates, so only the figures they agree on are shown here.

stories.title: HP jumps 11% and Deere reverses higher; Ambarella and Nutanix sink.
stories.body: HP Inc. rose **11.5%** after beating estimates ($0.83 vs $0.75 a share, revenue $16.0B vs $15.4B) and guiding fiscal 2027 EPS to $3.15–3.45 (StockTitan, Motley Fool, Longbridge). Deere closed **+4.4%** after falling about 3–4% before the open on EPS of $3.89 vs $4.05 expected and a fiscal 2027 net income forecast of $4.50–5.25B vs $5.91B expected (StockTitan, Reuters via WTAQ, The Fly). Dell finished +0.6% after trading down about 5% at midday despite its big beat and raise, an AI backlog of $132.3B and a $25B buyback; Workday rose 0.7% (StockTitan, Motley Fool via MyAllies). On the other side, Ambarella fell **19.8%** after guiding Q4 revenue to $70–75M from $115.2M in Q3, with its CEO citing memory prices, Nutanix fell **15.2%** as CEO Rajiv Ramaswami will step down, and Urban Outfitters lost 10.3% (StockTitan, The Fly). China's Kanzhun (+12.6%) and Li Auto (+11.0%) rose after their reports. Markets are closed Thursday and there are no major earnings Friday.

stories.title: Core PCE runs hot at 3.3%, GDP is revised up to 4.3% and new home sales jump 14%, keeping a December hike priced.
stories.body: October core PCE rose **0.3%** on the month as expected but **3.3%** on the year, above the 3.2% forecast and up from 3.1%; headline PCE rose 3.8% as expected and personal income jumped 0.7% (BEA via Unusual Whales, PANews). Q3 GDP was revised up to **4.3%** from 3.4%, durable goods rose 0.2% vs about 0.5% expected, and jobless claims fell to 189K (Breaking The News, InstaForex). New home sales jumped **14.2%** to a 701,000 rate in October vs 650,000 expected, the most since December 2025, though September was revised down to 614,000 from 676,000; the median price fell 3.2% from a year earlier to $391,300 and supply fell to 8.0 months (Commerce Department via Reuters/WHBL, Anadolu). The Fed's Beige Book said 8 of 12 districts grew slightly to moderately and 4 were flat; "prices increased moderately overall," input costs "generally outpaced" selling prices, and wages rose moderately, "an uptick" from the prior report (Federal Reserve). The 10Y fell about 6bp to 4.85%. CME FedWatch had about 95% on a 25bp hike on December 9 as of Tuesday (Yahoo Finance); Kalshi has 25bp at **92%**, a hold at 5% and a bigger hike at 3% (Wed 11/25 close). The pre-meeting blackout starts Saturday.

stories.title: Oil heads for its first weekly gain in four weeks after a projectile hits Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery.
stories.body: Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery temporarily halted some operations after a projectile struck it on Thursday, killing a Nepalese worker and wounding several others, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said; it came a day after Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on the Ras Tanura refinery and the Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan (Reuters via Yahoo Finance and RTÉ). Brent gained nearly $2 on Thursday to settle at its highest since Nov 6 and was at **$97.71** at 2:45a Friday, up 1.2%; WTI, which had no Thursday settlement because of Thanksgiving, was at $86.27 then but had eased to **$84.60** by 8:37a, still up 1.1% from Wednesday (Reuters, site feed). Iranian attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz continue, and Ukraine has stepped up drone strikes on Russian refineries (Reuters). ANZ says Brent "can still push above $100 a barrel without another major escalation." OPEC+ meets Sunday, Nov 29, and is likely to keep its output targets for at least the first quarter of 2027, sources told Reuters.
